chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Salih, who said:

When my father died and the matter came to me, my father had upon the people promissory notes from the debtor’s wealth. So I wrote to him to inform him, and he wrote: “Demand it from them and exact repayment from them.”

So the people paid me, except for one man upon whom there was a promissory note for four hundred dinars. I came to him demanding it, but he delayed me, and his son treated me lightly and behaved foolishly toward me. So I complained to his father, and he said, “And what was that?” Then I seized his beard, took hold of his leg, dragged him to the middle of the house, and kicked him many times.

So his son went out crying for help to the people of Baghdad, saying: “A man from Qumm, a Rafidi, has killed my father!” Then a crowd of them gathered against me. So I mounted my animal and said: “Well done, O people of Baghdad! You side with the oppressor against the wronged stranger! I am a man from the people of Hamadan, from the people of the Sunnah, and this one attributes me to the people of Qumm and to rejection in order to take away my right and my wealth.”

He said: Then they turned against him and wanted to enter his shop, until I calmed them down. Then the owner of the promissory note appealed to me and swore by divorce that he would indeed pay me my money, until I got them away from him.

key_terms.الظَّالِمِ: the wrongdoer or oppressor in the dispute
key_terms.الْغَرِيمِ: the debtor whose liability is being claimed
key_terms.بِحَقِّي: my rightful due or legal claim
key_terms.حَانُوتِهِ: his shop or place of trade
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: a gold coin used as a unit of monetary value
key_terms.سَفَاتِجُ: promissory notes or financial instruments used to secure or transfer debt
key_terms.فَمَاطَلَنِي: he delayed me and procrastinated in repayment
key_terms.وَاسْتَقْضِ: seek to exact repayment or collect the due debt

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith from al-Kafi say about collecting unpaid debts and dealing with a debtor who refuses payment?
ai.summary: This narration describes the collection of financial dues after the death of the narrator’s father, under instruction to demand repayment from debtors. It recounts a confrontation with one debtor in Baghdad, showing the tension surrounding debt recovery, social identity, and public accusation in that setting.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Salih who said,

‘When my father died and the matter (of collecting dues on behalf of the 12<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) came upon me, there were promissory notes upon the people from the adversaries. So I wrote to him<sup>asws</sup> letting him<sup>asws</sup> know. So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘Demand from them and enforce upon them’.

So the people fulfilled (their debts) except for one man who had a promissory note upon him of four hundred Dinars. So I went over to him seeking it, but he stalled me and his son belittled with me and behaved foolishly. So I complained to his father, and he said, ‘So what was that anyway!’ So I grabbed his beard and seized him by his leg and dragged him to the middle of the house, and kicked him with a lot of kicks.

So his son went out yelling (for help) with the people of Baghdad and he was saying, ‘A Qummy, a Rafizi has killed my father!’ So some people from the gathered upon me, and I rode upon my animal and said, ‘Well done, O people of Baghdad (sarcastically)! You are inclining with the oppressor against the oppressed stranger? I am a man from the people of Hamdan from the Sunnis and this one is linking me to the people of Qumm and the Rafizis in order to go away with my right and my wealth’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So they inclined against him and they intended to enter into his shop until I calmed them down, and the owner of the promissory note requested to me and asked for an oath with the divorce that he would be paying me my wealth if I take them (the people) out from him’.
en.sarwar: 15. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Salih who has said the following.

“When my father died and the task (of working is representative of the Imams) was left to me with my father there were promissory notes from those who has said the following. owed (religious dues). I wrote to him (the Imam (a.s.) about the case. He wrote back to me, “Demand from them and make them pay.”

People paid what they owed except one man who had signed a promissory note for four hundred Dinars. I went to demand from him what he owed but he procrastinated and took it lightly and his behaved foolishly. I complained to his father and he said, “So what!” I then hold him by his beard and leg and pulled him towards the center of the house and kicked him many times.

His son went out and cried for help from the people of Baghdad saying, “He is a Qummi, Rafidi (derogatory name for Shi‘a) he has killed my father.” From the people of Baghdad many gathered around me. I rode my equine animal and said, “Very nice of you people of Baghdad. You support the unjust against a lonely stranger. I am a man from the sunni sect and he calls me a man from Qumm and a Rafidi so that he can destroy my rights.”

The narrator has said that people then turned against him and they wanted to enter his store. I then calmed them down. The signatory in the promissory note called me and set upon himself a stipulation with an oath that said, “His wife will be divorced if he did not pay his dues.” My part of the stipulation was to ask the people to leave his place.”
